reader.title: Lynching of John McKern
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: The wire brief says McKern was 'hanged by a mob' and the Denver dispatch says the robbed man's friends hanged him to a tree (A1, A2).

McKern was hanged without legal process by 'a mob' or the robbed man's 'friends' (A1, A2), and a Texas paper describes a mock trial by 'three free judges' before the hanging (A4), all for an alleged robbery. The victim's race is not given in any report.

Two differently worded dispatches, the wire brief (A1) and a Denver telegram (A2), agree that McKern was hanged at Lawson, Arizona, on 8 May for robbing a railroad man, and an independent Texas paragraph matches the place and day (A4).

summary.text: The lynching of John McKern was the hanging of a man from Bloomington, Illinois, by a mob at Lawson, Arizona, on Monday, 8 May 1882.
He was accused of robbing a railroad man, and the story ran as a brief wire item in eastern and southern papers, while Texas papers used it to remark on Arizona's rough justice.
According to the wire brief, McKern and others had assaulted and robbed a railroad hand at or near Lawson.
A Denver dispatch dated 8 May, relaying news from Lawson, named only McKern as the robber of a "railway man."
The Denver dispatch said the robbed man's friends caught McKern and "hanged him to a tree until he was dead."
The wire brief instead attributed the hanging to "a mob."

A Texas paragraph that did not name the victim described a "highwayman" captured at Lawson on Monday morning, "tried by three free judges, found guilty and hanged to a tree within the brief period of an hour."
The same paragraph said the hanging was carried out "without alarming the police."
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The Lancaster Daily Intelligencer ran the wire brief on 9 May among "Crime and Casualty" items, and the Savannah Morning News and the Cambria Freeman of Ebensburg, Pennsylvania, printed the same sentence on 11 and 12 May.
The Wheeling Register carried the Denver version on 9 May under the headline "Hanged for Robbery."
None of these items gave McKern's race or added comment.
The Brenham Weekly Banner treated the hanging ironically, calling Arizona "a dreary waste of sand hills and desert" where "a spirit of speedy and in expensive justice toward criminals" prevailed.
The Waco Daily Examiner reprinted that paragraph on 17 May.
Accounts differ on who did the hanging: "a mob" in the wire brief, the robbed man's "friends" in the Denver dispatch, and "three free judges" in the Texas paragraph.
They also differ on the accusation, since the wire brief said McKern acted with others while the Denver dispatch named him alone.

accounts.label: Wire brief
accounts.gist: McKern was hanged by a mob at Lawson because he and others had assaulted and robbed a railroad hand.

accounts.label: Denver dispatch
accounts.gist: News from Lawson said McKern robbed a railway man, whose friends caught him and hanged him to a tree until he was dead.

accounts.label: Texas editorial paragraph
accounts.gist: An unnamed highwayman captured at Lawson on Monday morning was tried by 'three free judges', found guilty and hanged to a tree within an hour, 'without alarming the police'.

framing.detail: Eastern and southern papers ran a one-sentence brief among crime and casualty items, with no comment.
The Wheeling Register headed the Denver dispatch 'Hanged for Robbery'.
The Brenham Banner mocked Arizona as 'a dreary waste' while crediting it with 'speedy and inexpensive justice toward criminals', an ironic tone that neither condemns nor plainly endorses the hanging.

versions.value: three free judges after a summary trial

conflicts.note: The versions are compatible (a small group of the victim's friends acting as a mob) but differ in wording; none comes from a local Arizona source.
